project.name: Online Food Delivery Platform
project.summary: A web platform for customers to order food, restaurants to manage menus, and delivery partners to fulfill orders.

functional_requirements: Add items to cart and place orders
Manage restaurants, menus, and orders by administrators
non_functional_requirements: Response time under 2 seconds for user actions
High availability and reliable data storage

actors.name: Customer
actors.description: Registers, logs in, browses restaurants, orders food, and tracks delivery.

actors.name: Restaurant Administrator
actors.description: Creates and updates restaurant profiles, menus, food items, and handles incoming orders.

actors.name: Delivery Partner
actors.description: Views assigned deliveries, updates delivery status, and completes deliveries.

use_cases.name: Register and Login
use_cases.description: Customer creates an account and authenticates to access the platform.

use_cases.name: Browse Restaurants and Menus
use_cases.description: Customer searches and views restaurant listings and their menus.

use_cases.name: Place Order and Pay
use_cases.description: Customer adds items to cart, confirms order, and completes online payment.

use_cases.name: Manage Restaurant Catalog
use_cases.description: Administrator adds, edits, or removes restaurant details, menus, and food items.

use_cases.name: Update Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Delivery partner marks deliveries as picked up, in‑transit, or completed.

criteria: Password must be stored hashed with a strong algorithm
Login fails after 5 consecutive invalid attempts
Restaurant list loads within 2 seconds
Menu items display correct price and availability

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Add items to cart and place orders
criteria: Cart persists across sessions for logged‑in users
Order confirmation email is sent within 1 minute
Payment gateway returns success/failure within 3 seconds
Sensitive payment data is never stored in plain text

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Manage restaurants, menus, and orders by administrators
criteria: Administrator actions are logged with timestamp and user ID
Changes to menu are reflected to customers within 5 seconds

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to register and login, so that I can securely access the platform.
acceptance_criteria: User can create an account with email verification.
User can log in using email and password and receive an authentication token.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to browse restaurants and view menus, so that I can choose what to order.
acceptance_criteria: Restaurants are listed with basic info and can be filtered by cuisine.
Selecting a restaurant displays its menu with item details and prices.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to add items to a cart and place an order, so that I can purchase food.
acceptance_criteria: Items can be added, updated, or removed from the cart before checkout.
Order submission records the cart contents, total amount, and generates an order ID.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to make online payments, so that my order is confirmed instantly.
acceptance_criteria: Payment gateway accepts credit/debit cards and returns success or failure.
Order status changes to 'Paid' only after successful payment confirmation.

user_stories.story: As a restaurant administrator, I want to manage menus and incoming orders, so that I can keep offerings up‑to‑date and fulfill orders.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create, edit, or delete menu items and set availability.
Admin can view a list of new orders, update order status, and mark orders as ready.

user_stories.story: As a delivery partner, I want to view assigned deliveries and update delivery status, so that customers can track their orders.
acceptance_criteria: Delivery partner sees a list of assigned orders with pickup and drop‑off details.
Partner can change status to 'Picked Up' and 'Delivered', triggering customer notifications.

UML Generator.use_case:
flowchart LR
    User -->|register/login| AuthSystem
    User -->|browse| WebApp
    User -->|place order| OrderSystem
    RestaurantAdmin -->|manage| AdminPortal
    DeliveryPartner -->|update status| DeliverySystem
    AuthSystem -->|authenticate| Database
    OrderSystem -->|process| Database
    DeliverySystem -->|track| Database
UML Generator.sequence:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant WA as WebApp
    participant AS as AuthService
    participant OS as OrderService
    participant DB as Database
    participant DP as DeliveryPartner
    U->>WA: login credentials
    WA->>AS: authenticate
    AS->>DB: verify user
    DB-->>AS: user data
    AS-->>WA: auth token
    WA->>U: login success
    U->>WA: add items to cart
    U->>WA: place order
    WA->>OS: create order
    OS->>DB: store order
    DB-->>OS: orderId
    OS-->>WA: order confirmation
    OS->>DP: assign delivery
    DP->>OS: accept
    OS->>DP: delivery details
    DP->>OS: update status
    OS->>WA: order status update
    WA->>U: order status

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    password_hash TEXT,
    phone TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Restaurants (
    restaurant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    address TEXT,
    phone TEXT,
    admin_user_id INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (admin_user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE MenuItems (
    item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    restaurant_id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    price REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (restaurant_id) REFERENCES Restaurants(restaurant_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    restaurant_id INTEGER,
    delivery_partner_id INTEGER,
    order_time DATETIME,
    status TEXT,
    total REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (restaurant_id) REFERENCES Restaurants(restaurant_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (delivery_partner_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

Project Structure.architecture: A micro‑service style system with a React/Vite SPA communicating over HTTPS to FastAPI services. FastAPI handles user, restaurant, order, and delivery domains, persisting data in PostgreSQL. Redis caches session and menu data. RabbitMQ decouples order processing and delivery notifications. JWT secures API calls. Nginx terminates TLS and serves the SPA. Docker containers are orchestrated via Docker Compose (or Kubernetes) for scalability and resilience.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        UI[React SPA]
    end
    subgraph API
        Auth[Auth Service]
        User[User Service]
        Restaurant[Restaurant Service]
        Order[Order Service]
        Delivery[Delivery Service]
    end
    subgraph Infra
        DB[(PostgreSQL)]
        Cache[(Redis)]
        MQ[(RabbitMQ)]
        NG[NGINX]
    end
    UI -->|HTTPS| NG
    NG -->|Proxy| Auth & User & Restaurant & Order & Delivery
    Auth -->|JWT| User
    Order -->|Publish| MQ
    MQ -->|Consume| Delivery
    Delivery -->|Update| DB
    User --> DB
    Restaurant --> DB
    Order --> DB
    Cache -->|Cache| DB

Documentation.readme: Online Food Delivery Platform enables users to register, browse restaurants, add items to cart, place orders, pay online, and track deliveries. Restaurants manage menus and orders; delivery partners handle assigned deliveries and update status. Built with React front‑end, Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL, JWT auth, and Stripe for payments.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /api/auth/register – body {email,password,role}. Returns JWT. POST /api/auth/login – returns JWT. GET /api/restaurants – list restaurants. GET /api/restaurants/:id/menu – menu items. POST /api/cart – add item. GET /api/cart – view cart. POST /api/orders – place order, includes payment token. GET /api/orders/:id – order status. PUT /api/delivery/:id/status – update status (partner only). Admin routes prefixed /api/admin for CRUD on restaurants, menus, items.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` in root and client directories. Set up PostgreSQL DB and run migrations (`npm run migrate`). Create .env with DB_URL, JWT_SECRET, STRIPE_KEY. Start server with `npm run dev`. Launch client with `npm start` in client folder.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker. Use docker-compose to run app, db, and nginx. Deploy to any cloud VM or Kubernetes. Configure environment variables securely. Set up HTTPS via Let’s Encrypt. Use PM2 or systemd to keep Node process alive.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Auth, user registration/login, JWT. Sprint 2: Restaurant listing, menu API, admin CRUD. Sprint 3: Cart management, order creation, Stripe integration. Sprint 4: Delivery partner UI, status updates, real‑time tracking via WebSocket. Sprint 5: UI polish, performance testing, CI/CD pipeline.
Documentation.architecture: Three‑tier: React SPA (client) → Node.js/Express REST API (service) → PostgreSQL (data). JWT secures endpoints. Stripe handles payments. WebSocket server pushes order status to users and partners. Nginx reverse proxy serves static assets and routes API. Docker isolates each component.
